title: The Smoothing Specter
intro: Everything from Week 7: GNN modules, over-smoothing, skip connections, graph manipulation, prediction heads, metrics, splits and link prediction.

questions.prompt: Part 1. With $K=2$, how many nodes are in the receptive field of node 10 (interior of the path)?
questions.scenario: **Scenario A (receptive fields on a path graph).** A long path graph $\dots-1-2-3-4-5-\dots$ with a $K$-layer GNN. The receptive field of a node is its $K$-hop neighbourhood (a node and everything within $K$ hops).

questions.prompt: Part 2. With $K=2$, how many nodes are shared by the receptive fields of node 10 and node 13 (distance 3)?
questions.scenario: **Scenario A (receptive fields on a path graph).** A long path graph $\dots-1-2-3-4-5-\dots$ with a $K$-layer GNN. The receptive field of a node is its $K$-hop neighbourhood (a node and everything within $K$ hops).

questions.prompt: Part 3. Raising $K$ to 8 for both nodes makes their embeddings:
options: More different, since each sees more of the graph
More similar, since their receptive fields overlap more: the over-smoothing effect
questions.explanation: Highly overlapped receptive fields give highly similar embeddings.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly contrasts the two data-splitting settings?
options: Transductive: whole graph visible, labels split. Inductive: edges between splits broken, test on unseen graphs
Transductive: edges broken. Inductive: whole graph visible
questions.explanation: Friends leaking answers vs separate classes.

questions.prompt: *“In link prediction I also pass the supervision edges to the GNN as message edges.”*
options: Supervision edges are the answers and must not be fed into the GNN
Message and supervision edges are the same

questions.prompt: $N=3$ skip connections give how many paths?
After adding a virtual node connected to all nodes, any two nodes are at distance:

options: Dropout at test time uses all neurons
Batch norm re-centres to zero mean and re-scales to unit variance
Global sum pooling is independent of the number of nodes
Edge head can be Linear(Concat($h_v$,$h_u$)) or a dot product
questions.explanation: Sum pooling grows with graph size; mean is size-normalised.

questions.prompt: *“99% accuracy proves my classifier finds nearly all positives.”*
options: With rare positives, accuracy is dominated by TN; recall can be low
